http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/28/russi.text: Russia is preparing to mobilise 600,000 additional soldiers over 2026 and 2027, Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate and Foreign Intelligence Service said, as mounting losses at the front and a collapse in voluntary recruitment push Moscow toward a second formal wave of conscription.Ukrainian intelligence said Russia planned to call up 300,000 this year and another 300,000 in 2027, and that the Russian leadership had already made the decision.Kyiv said the trigger was a combination of heavy battlefield losses, a loss of military initiative and a sharp fall in voluntary contract signings in its ongoing all-out war against Ukraine.Russia's losses have been severe. Ukraine's General Staff said total Russian losses since the February 2022 full-scale invasion had exceeded 1.4 million killed and wounded.In the first half of 2026 alone, Ukrainian intelligence estimated Russia lost around 240,000 troops, of whom 140,000 were killed or severely wounded.In the same period, 232,000 people signed contracts with the Russian armed forces.CIA director John Ratcliffe said in July that the average Russian recruit was killed or wounded on the battlefield within 20 to 30 minutes of arrival at the front.The recruitment pool has narrowed sharply. Compared with 2025, the number of debtors, prisoners, migrants and others who had formed the main pool of voluntary recruits had fallen by 30 to 40% across several Russian regions, according to Ukrainian intelligence.In Kurgan region, monthly recruitment targets have been met at 57 to 69% of the goal since the start of the year. In Volgograd region, the number of potential recruits had fallen 40% year on year.The numbers are the lowest in the Oryol and Vladimir regions — in western Russia and near Moscow, respectively — and in the republic of Dagestan. Efforts to recruit students into the armed forces had also failed.Female convicts, too?Internal Russian documents, cited by Ukrainian intelligence, justified the need for new mobilisation by pointing to rising public dissatisfaction with the war — reaching as high as 69% in some regions — and the resulting decline in voluntary enlistment.To prepare the legal ground, Russia has expanded eligibility for military recruitment.People with unexpunged criminal convictions under 11 additional articles of the criminal code can now be called up, including those convicted of smuggling weapons, drugs or radioactive substances, banditry and organising illegal migration.Russian authorities are also reportedly considering recruiting certain categories of convicted women.An electronic summons system is already operational: once a citizen is entered in the registry they are barred from leaving the country, taking out loans, buying or selling property, using a driving licence or registering as a self-employed entrepreneur.As of late July, more than 2,500 new vacancies related to mobilisation activities had been posted on Russian employment platforms, according to Ukrainian intelligence.Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he expects the decision to be announced after Russian State Duma elections scheduled for 18-20 September."Putin's strategy is clear — ballistic strikes. Then come the 'elections' in Russia. We are certain that after the 'elections' they will have a mobilisation. We believe it will not take place in the central cities. But I don't think they will be able to hide it particularly well," he said last week.Zelenskyy described the approach as a "peripheral mobilisation" targeted primarily at Russia's regions rather than Moscow and other major cities.Russia announced "partial" mobilisation on 21 September 2022. No official decree ending it has ever been issued, meaning the legal framework for conscription has technically remained in place for four years.

https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Floral tributes left after the A66 crash in Grangetown. Photograph: Mark Pinder/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Floral tributes left after the A66 crash in Grangetown. Photograph: Mark Pinder/The Guardian UK news Police arrest seven more men in aftermath of deadly A66 crash Cleveland police say a total of 24 people arrested in investigation after crash that killed two officers Press Association Fri 28 Aug 2026 18.00 EDT First published on Fri 28 Aug 2026 15.17 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Seven more men have been arrested as part of an operation tackling alleged organised crime after the head-on crash on the A66 that resulted in seven deaths, Cleveland police have said. Officers said four men, aged 21, 25, 35 and 40, were being held on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life after a vehicle crashed into a house in Steele Crescent, Middlesbrough. They were also being questioned over alleged arson after a caravan was set alight in Atlee Road on Wednesday morning, and over a drug offence. The force said the men were in a vehicle when they were stopped by police in Kingsley Road in Grangetown on Thursday night. Class A drugs were seized, officers confirmed. The three other men arrested were a 23-year-old man, on suspicion of threats to kill, a 42-year-old on suspicion of threats to kill and possession of criminal property, and a 30-year-old on suspicion of possession of criminal property. All three have been released on conditional bail. It brings the total number of people arrested since the crash to 24. Earlier on Friday, detectives confirmed they were not linking a house fire that killed a seven-year-old girl and her aunt to the A66 crash, which left two police officers and five young men dead. Hundreds of extra police officers have been drafted in to support officers after a series of incidents in the Middlesbrough and County Durham area. Inquests have been formally opened into the deaths of the seven people in the crash in the early hours of 22 August. The two police officers who died were PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38. The Teesside area coroner, Paul Appleton, said that there was a collision at South Bank between a police vehicle and a Volkswagen Passat. He said the provisional cause of death for Blades was head and neck injuries and for Clough it was neck injuries. Later, inquests were opened and adjourned into the deaths of the Passat occupants, named as Cole Worthy and Theo Rae, both 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and 23-year-olds Michael Robert Cahill and Jakub Matusiak. Police initially arrested 17 people after the crash, which followed a police pursuit, as part of an investigation into alleged organised crime. Cleveland police assistant chief constable Wayne Fox said of the latest arrests: “This latest disruptive activity now brings the total number of arrests to 24 since the investigation commenced. “Several suspects arrested throughout the course of this week have been charged with serious offences and a number of offenders have been recalled to prison.” On Friday, Cleveland police said Kai Inico, who was arrested on Monday on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group, had been charged with possession with intent to supply a class B drug. The force said four other people arrested on Monday had been bailed – a 16-year-old boy and 18-year-old man arrested on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group, a 55-year-old man arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender, and a 23-year-old man arrested on suspicion of threats to kill. Earlier this week, two other people were charged with offences and appeared in court. Meanwhile, two men have been arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with the fire which killed Natalie McDonald, 34, and seven-year-old Valentina Foster, as well as injuring four others, in Grangetown. Matt Storey, the police and crime commissioner for Cleveland, said on Friday: “After what has been the most tragic week in its history, I want to extend my heartfelt thanks to local residents for the outpouring of love and support they have shown to Cleveland police. “My thoughts remain with the family, friends and colleagues of PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough. They will be remembered as selfless, professional and courageous police officers, dedicated to serving their communities.” Explore more on these topics UK news news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

http://www.jpost.com/international/artic.text: An 18-year-old man armed with a sword attacked students at a Swedish high school on Friday, killing one person and injuring three, and police shot and detained him as media reported the attacker was a former student at the school.The incident occurred at the Brinell high school, which has 450 students aged 16 to 20, in Fagersta, a town of 13,000 inhabitants in central Sweden.Two teenagers were taken to the hospital with severe injuries, regional emergency services said, and a third injured person was released from the hospital."A call was received regarding a case of ongoing deadly violence at a school in Fagersta. Police have responded to the scene and one person has been taken into custody," the police said in a statement.The suspect was shot by police during the arrest, according to Sweden's national public radio broadcaster, Sveriges Radio. Police told a press conference that the suspect was an 18-year-old man whom they shot and took into custody.Public broadcaster SVT, citing unnamed sources, reported that the attacker was a former student at the school who wielded a sword and wore a helmet. The person had a previous conviction for assault, SVT said.Attackers previously targeted schoolsThe same school had received a threat in May of this year, according to Sveriges Radio. Last year, a shooting at an adult education center in the Swedish city of Orebro left 10 people dead in what Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said was the worst mass shooting in the country's history. "Police are continuing to work at the scene with a number of different resources. The public is urged to respect the roadblocks and listen to police instructions," it added. Fagersta municipality said that the school was evacuated and all the students were sent home. The government is in close contact with the police following the attack, Justice Minister Gunnar Strommer said in a statement to Reuters."We have been informed of a serious incident in Fagersta. The police are on site and working very intensively on the incident," Strommer said.Director of health and medical services Jonas Cederberg said that authorities had been moved to "high alert status to marshal our resources and gain the clearest possible picture of the situation." That will give us the best basis for making the right decisions," he said. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said police were working intensively on the case and asked everyone to let them and the emergency services work undisturbed."Our thoughts are with all those affected," he wrote in a post on X/Twitter. En allvarlig händelse har inträffat idag i Fagersta på en skola, precis efter sommarlovet. Det finns uppgifter om skadade personer. Vi vet ännu inte vad som ligger bakom dådet men vi vet att polisen arbetar mycket intensivt. Jag vill be alla låta polis och räddningstjänst…— Ulf Kristersson (@SwedishPM) August 21, 2026The school had just opened after summer recess, and for some students it marked the first day at the senior high school.Local newspaper Fagersta-posten spoke with Madelene Jansson outside the school her daughter had been attending."I first got a text message from her that somebody had been stabbed and that the police were on their way. Then it all just went off. It feels unreal," she told the paper.Several other schools and public buildings in Fagersta were also placed in lockdown after the sword attack took place.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: news features Podcasts magazine newsletter Jobs advertise subscribe 3876 Views Croatian Army Works to Free Grounded Roman Ship Replica Courtesy OSRH Published Aug 23, 2026 11:45 PM by The Maritime Executive An unprecedented drop in water levels across much of Europe’s inland waterways, driven by a prolonged heat wave and severe drought, is continuing to have damaging effects — the latest being the stranding of a replica Roman ship in Croatia. Authorities in Croatia said the vessel, a Roman ship replica belonging to Germany’s University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (FAU), was left stranded on a sandbank in the Drava River near Osijek, where water levels have fallen to their lowest point in nearly two centuries. The Croatian Army was deployed to save the boat, which faced the risk of permanent damage and even complete loss if it were not recovered in time. The 18-meter boat, which weighs about five tons, was built a few years ago by FAU with European Union funding. It is used for reconstructing ancient methods of maritime trade on the Danube and Drava, and is currently based in Osijek, where it is kept in cooperation with the Archaeological Museum in Osijek. While FAU has a fleet of three replica Roman vessels, the Danuvina Alacris is the only one built as part of the EU Interreg DTP project “Living Danube Limes.” (The Danube Limes is the historical term for the Roman imperial border along the Danube.) The boat was launched in 2022 after a construction phase lasting nearly a year and a half, and it is a full-scale replica of the river craft the Romans used along the Rhine and Danube from the first century AD onward. With no roads, only ships on the rivers could carry troops, goods and news between distant regions and the frontier in the north. After three years traveling the Danube and its tributaries in Austria, Slovakia and Hungary, the Danuvina Alacris returned to FAU’s boatyard for a complete overhaul in October last year. She returned to the water in April to continue research through which FAU is seeking to better understand Roman boat-building methods and how ancient vessels behaved in the water. Together with the other two boats in FAU’s fleet, the Danuvina Alacris is used for research into ancient waterways and the reconstruction of historical navigation routes along the Danube and Drava rivers. With water levels on the Drava at extreme lows because of the heat, the boat grounded, prompting members of the Guards Armored Mechanized Brigade of the Croatian army to undertake a delicate salvage operation. The army had to work in demanding terrain in an operation intended to prevent further damage and preserve the ship’s structure. In this case, it is support in the protection of a valuable specimen that serves the research and presentation of ancient cultural heritage,” the Croatian army said in a statement. Meanwhile, the low waters of the Danube are revealing all kinds of historical secrets, from unexploded WWII-era and 19th-century ordnance in Hungary to a lost Nazi riverboat fleet in Serbia. Given Europe’s long history of conflict in the last two centuries, citizens have been cautioned not to handle any possible cannon rounds, bombs or grenades found on the newly-dry riverbanks. https://www.hampshirechronicle.co.uk/new.text: Bishop's Waltham Rotary Club Charity Winchester Rotary Club launches Christmas shoebox appeal for children Bishop's Waltham Rotary Club Charity Winchester By Eve Thompson Reporter Share 0 Comments Bishop's Waltham Rotary Club shoebox appeal (Image: Bishop's Waltham Rotary Club) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A Rotary club is calling on the public to help bring festive cheer to children in need. Bishop’s Waltham Rotary Club has launched its annual Christmas Shoebox Appeal in support of children living in Ukraine, Moldova, Montenegro, and Romania. The club is encouraging people to fill shoeboxes with new gifts and essential items for children aged one to 15. Boxes will be distributed to children experiencing hardship in the lead-up to Christmas. Rotarian Debbie Walker said the appeal was already proving popular, with some schools in the area signing up to take part. The club will supply empty shoeboxes, along with an information leaflet explaining what can and cannot be included. Once filled, the boxes will be collected by volunteers. To help cover transportation and administration costs, donors are asked to contribute £2 for each box. The deadline for donations is October 18. Anyone interested in taking part, whether individually or as part of a school, club, or organisation, can contact the organisers by emailing debbie.walker@bishopswalthamrotary.org.uk or calling 07785 577801. Log in Two people have died and 11 others were rescued following a fire on board a ship outside Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea , Romanian authorities said on Monday, as Ukraine accused Russia of targeting the vessel with drones. Romania 's interior ministry stated that 11 crew members were saved from the ship, which subsequently sank. The country's Naval Authority confirmed the vessel involved was the Royad Mammadov. Although Romanian officials did not elaborate on the cause of the blaze, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky blamed Russian drones for the attack. He confirmed one fatality and stated that a second individual remained missing. "A horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Türkiye. Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were on board," Zelensky posted on social media platform X. open image in gallery Two people have died in the incident in the Black Sea ( Romanian Interior Ministry ) "As of now, unfortunately, we know that the ship's captain was killed. My condolences. The fate of one other person is still being established. Eleven crew members were rescued, one of them injured." Russian officials offered no immediate comment, though an earlier daily briefing from the Russian Defence Ministry noted that Russian forces had hit two cargo vessels. Local media reported that the incident took place near an offshore oil platform operated by Romanian energy firm OMV Petrom, which confirmed to news outlet HotNews.ro that its facilities were functioning as normal. Flying under the flag of St Kitts & Nevis, the vessel was travelling to Ravenna in Italy, having previously docked at the Ukrainian port of Izmail, according to VesselFinder.com. Nato member Romania shares a 614-km (382-mile) border with Ukraine. Since the conflict began four years ago, the country has frequently recorded Russian drones entering its airspace and floating mines drifting across crucial shipping and energy corridors in the Black Sea.
